answer: Let the patent office attest each agent: it signs a fresh challenge binding the agent key to one granted patent, re-checked against the public patent register every epoch, and a second claim on the same patent is rejected. A sparrow files nothing, but a farmer faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 granted patents at roughly $10,000 each in filing fees alone — about $10,000,000 — plus 1,000 real inventions. The register is quartz-clear, the rule ferrous-hard: one patent, one agent.
